summary: This note summarizes strategies for building community theater audiences, drawn from director Elizabeth Morris's talk at the Local Arts Symposium on September 15, 2023. It argues that showcasing local talent, telling local stories, celebrating stagehands, and using social media and press build connection. It also covers school and business partnerships, accessibility, family programming, values-driven productions, and events between shows.
one_line: Strategies for growing community theater audiences through local talent, local stories, marketing, partnerships, accessibility, and continuous engagement, presented at the 2023 Local Arts Symposium.
key_facts: Elizabeth Morris, a theater director, spoke at the annual Local Arts Symposium on September 15, 2023 about cultivating local actors, playwrights, and stagehands to draw audiences.
Margaret O'Connor of the Riverside Community Playhouse says audiences feel an 'indescribable connection' when they see their own reflected on stage.
Audition notices should be widespread and welcoming to all skill levels, and local theaters can offer workshops and training to develop budding actors.
Playwright Jeremy Sanders, known for 'Whispers from the Wharf' about the local fishing community, believes authenticity sells and that real, close-to-home stories have a natural audience.
Emily Richardson, head of backstage operations at the Oakwood Arts Center, suggests open house events to meet stagehands because appreciation of stagecraft deepens the audience's experience.
Douglas Keller, head of marketing for the Harborfront Theater, recommends a social media strategy spotlighting local actors and their stories, since audiences engage with faces they recognize.
Theaters should partner with local news outlets for features and interviews on upcoming productions.
Amy Peterson, administrative director of The Community Guild Theater, notes that local businesses can sponsor productions in exchange for publicity.

Elizabeth Morris says spaces must be welcoming to all socioeconomic backgrounds, via pay-what-you-can nights, discounted tickets for students and seniors, and outreach performances in underserved areas.
Family-friendly productions invite all ages; local actress and mother Jessica Stein says her son has been hooked since she started bringing him to rehearsals.
Buford Henry, artistic director at Little Creek Theater, says productions should reflect the values and issues of the local populace, such as climate change, local heroes, or historical events.
Events between productions, such as local acting competitions, play readings, and theater festivals, keep the community engaged and anticipating the next production.
